_comment: Continuous demonstration simulation (src/simulation_engine.py). EVERY reading it produces is FABRICATED and labelled SIMULATED LIVE: it is not a Central Water Commission observation and can never authorize a real-world action. Each tick (every tick_seconds of real time) advances the SIMULATION clock by simulated_minutes_per_tick and produces readings_per_tick new river readings (every 15 simulated minutes by default), one hour of rainfall and a fresh traffic snapshot, all of which go through the normal River Agent validation/QC, Risk Assessment Engine, Evidence Layer, Disaster State Manager and capability control. A scenario sets the physical conditions the generator drives towards (target river level, rainfall), never the disaster state: every session starts in NORMAL and the state changes only through the state manager's own rules. The station UPPER_ANICUT_SIM is a twin of UPPER_ANICUT that reuses the real station's QC rules; the thresholds below are TEST/RESEARCH values, NOT official warning or danger levels. The state record lives in memory with scope 'simulated' and is never written to the real state file.

UPPER_ANICUT_SIM.reference: TEST VALUES - not official; chosen above the 2021-2025 CWC telemetry's usual high-flow band (about 74.8-75.0 m RL) for software testing only

scenarios._comment: Deterministic profiles. Underlying level: base(t+dt) = base + clamp(response_per_hour x (target_level_m - base) x dt, -max_fall, +max_rise). Reading = base + wave_m x sin(2 pi t / wave_period_hours) + noise (deterministic per session and timestamp, at most noise_m). Rain intensity relaxes towards rain_mm_per_hour at rain_response_per_hour; each hour varies deterministically by up to rain_variability. Traffic entries are hours since the scenario was selected. Target levels are chosen against the TEST thresholds above (warning 75.0 m, danger 75.6 m, recovery level 74.8 m = warning - 0.2 m).

NORMAL.label: Normal
NORMAL.description: Stable river well below the TEST warning level, with small natural fluctuations; light rain.

ALERT.label: Alert
ALERT.description: River rising gradually towards and across the TEST warning level (not the danger level), with small fluctuations; heavy rain observed and forecast.

EMERGENCY.label: Emergency
EMERGENCY.description: River rising substantially above the TEST danger level to a sustained peak; heavy rain with an extremely heavy forecast; riverside evacuation road closed.

RECOVERY.label: Recovery
RECOVERY.description: River declining gradually from an elevated level, with fluctuations; rain easing; the closed road reopens after 4 simulated hours. At an already normal level the river simply stays low.

cycle.label: Full flood cycle (automatic)
cycle.description: Conditions move NORMAL -> ALERT -> EMERGENCY -> RECOVERY on a fixed simulated-hour schedule. The disaster state follows only when the evidence satisfies the state manager's rules.
